transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time feeling like I deserve the trust people put in me. I’m a physician, and I keep replaying little things from clinical work—minor imperfections, probably—and it starts to feel like proof that I’m not safe, or that I’m a dangerous doctor. I know that may sound excessive, but it’s been hard to shake.
Do you find yourself having persistent, intrusive thoughts that cause you anxiety, and do you feel the need to perform certain behaviors or mental acts in response to those thoughts?

I’m not sure I’d call it that, exactly. I mean, I do get stuck on thoughts and I can ruminate, but I don’t think I have… rituals or anything like that. Not in the sense of having to do a certain behavior to make the thought go away.

I guess I’m trying to answer that correctly—there are anxious thoughts, but I haven’t noticed compulsions, if that’s what you mean.
Do you find yourself feeling intense anxiety or fear in specific situations, or around certain things, where you feel like you might lose control or something terrible might happen?

I don’t think so, not in a specific phobia kind of way. I mean, I can get anxious, but I wouldn’t say there’s a particular place or object where I feel like I’m going to lose control or something awful will happen.

Does that answer what you mean?
Do you find yourself feeling anxious most days, even when there’s no clear reason or specific situation causing it?

I don’t think it’s most days, no. I mean, I can feel unsettled or tense sometimes, but it usually feels connected to something I’m thinking about, not just free-floating anxiety for no reason.

I hope that makes sense—I’m not trying to minimize it, but I wouldn’t describe myself as anxious all the time.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things going wrong in your work, even when there’s no clear reason to think they will—like making a mistake or harming someone unintentionally?

Yeah… I do worry about that at work. I try not to make it sound bigger than it is, because I know logically I check things carefully.

But even when I’ve reviewed the chart and there’s nothing showing anything bad happened, I can get stuck believing that some routine delay, or maybe a message I worded imperfectly, has quietly harmed a patient somehow. And then I think eventually everyone is going to find out.

I know that probably sounds… excessive. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Do you feel like your worries about work are something you can control, or do they feel intrusive and difficult to manage, almost like they take on a life of their own?

I wish I could say I can control it better. I mean, I try to reason through it—I review the chart, I look for evidence, and there usually isn’t anything there.

But it doesn’t really let go. It’s like I keep coming back to this belief that some routine delay, or some message I didn’t word perfectly, harmed a patient in a way I just haven’t found yet. And then I start thinking people are eventually going to discover it.

I know that may sound kind of irrational, and I’m not trying to be dramatic, but yes… it feels intrusive and hard to manage.

Are these worrisome thoughts about harming patients something you feel are intrusive and unwanted, almost like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to, and do they feel different from just normal concern or responsibility you’d expect in your job?

Yes… I think they are unwanted. I don’t sit down and decide to worry about it, and I know concern is part of the job.

But this feels different from just being careful. Even if I review the chart and there’s no evidence anything bad happened, I still keep coming back to this idea that some routine delay, or something I wrote imperfectly in a message, quietly harmed a patient. And then I start thinking it’s only a matter of time before everyone finds out.

I know that sounds like more than normal responsibility. I’m trying to answer this accurately.
Do these thoughts cause you significant distress or interfere with your ability to function in your daily work or personal life?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still functioning, mostly. I’m still showing up to clinic and doing what I need to do.

But I guess it has started to affect things. I’ve had to ask for help with some non-urgent administrative work, which I don’t love admitting, because I feel like I should be able to keep up with that. And outside of work, I’ve been avoiding social plans more. Partly because I don’t really trust my judgment or my energy right now.

So… yes, it’s distressing. I don’t think I’m falling apart, exactly, but it’s making me less reliable than I’d like to be, and more disconnected from people. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, trouble sleeping, or muscle tension, or mental symptoms like trouble concentrating or irritability, that seem to go along with these anxious thoughts?

Mostly concentration, I think. I don’t want to overstate it, because I am still getting through the day, but… I’ll read the same lab result or inbox message five times and still feel unsure what I just read.

Then something simple, like a non-urgent admin decision, can take me an embarrassing amount of time because I keep second-guessing whether I understood it correctly. I know that probably sounds inefficient more than anything, but it does seem to go along with the anxious thoughts. Is that the kind of mental symptom you mean?

Do these intrusive thoughts about possibly harming patients take up a lot of your time or mental energy, like thinking about them for more than an hour a day or feeling like you can’t move on until you’ve reviewed everything again and again?

I… yes, it can take up a lot of mental space. I don’t know if I’ve timed it exactly, so I don’t want to exaggerate, but it’s not just a quick worry and then I move on.

I’ll review the chart, and logically there won’t be anything showing a bad outcome, but I still keep feeling like some routine delay or some imperfectly worded message from me must have harmed someone somehow. And then I get stuck on the idea that eventually people will realize it.

I do go back over things again because it feels like I can’t quite trust that I’ve checked enough. I know that may sound excessive… but yes, it does pull me back in more than I’d like.
Do you feel personally responsible or guilty for these potential harms you worry about, even if you logically know you did everything correctly?

Yes… I do. I mean, logically I can usually tell myself that I followed the right steps, or that a small delay or an imperfect message doesn’t automatically mean I hurt someone.

But emotionally it doesn’t feel that way. I keep replaying these little clinical imperfections like they’re evidence that I’m not safe to be trusted. And I know that sounds dramatic, maybe unfair to myself, but… I think part of why I’m here is that I feel like I don’t really deserve the trust people put in me.

So yes, there’s guilt. More than I’d like to admit.

The presentation is most consistent with OCD (F42).
